THE LIGHT CAFÉ · SCIENTIFIC BACKGROUND

The Light Café: a field study of morning light.

A planned adaptive field study of morning light exposure, circadian phase, sleep and cognition in Tübingen, Germany.

Study design ↓
SETTINGTübingen, GermanyMobile research trailer
TIMINGNovember 2026 – February 2027Planned data collection
STATUSStudy in developmentProtocol details to follow

01 / THE RESEARCH QUESTION

How does morning light
affect circadian timing?

How do light intensity and spectral composition shape the human circadian response in everyday settings?

The Light Café is a proposed field study combining controlled morning light exposure with circadian, behavioural and subjective outcome measures. It asks how responses vary across light conditions and between individuals.

A mobile research trailer, planned for the forecourt of Tübingen’s main railway station, will serve as both an intervention space and a meeting place for researchers and the public.

The long-term aim is to inform biologically grounded, more personalised light interventions. These are research objectives, not established outcomes of this project.

02 / PLANNED STUDY DESIGN

The study
at a glance.

Sequential cohorts with light conditions
adapted in response to previous observations.

10weekday sessions
per participant
60minutes per session
over two weeks
144–192planned participants
across 6–8 cohorts
  1. BASELINE

    Baseline
    measurements

    Assess circadian phase with dim-light melatonin onset (DLMO), alongside actigraphy and cognitive performance measures.

  2. INTERVENTION

    Morning light
    sessions

    Ten one-hour sessions on weekdays, within four daily time windows between 07:00 and 11:00. Light intensity and spectral composition are controlled.

  3. FOLLOW-UP

    Repeat assessments
    and analyse the data.

    Repeat the assessments and collect subjective tiredness and well-being measures. Analyse each cohort to inform subsequent light conditions.

Up to six participants per time window and up to 24 per cohort are planned. The sample range is an operational recruitment estimate in the project proposal, not a reported power calculation. Exact light settings, eligibility criteria, allocation procedures and adaptation rules are not yet specified here.

03 / OUTCOME DOMAINS

What we plan
to measure.

Circadian, behavioural
and subjective measures.

Circadian phase DLMO
Timing of the evening rise in melatonin under dim-light conditions, measured before and after the intervention.
Sleep and activity ACTIGRAPHY
Objective assessment of rest–activity patterns using a wearable sensor.
Cognition PERFORMANCE
Tasks assessing cognitive performance and attention alongside the physiological measurements.
Daily experience SELF-REPORT
Subjective tiredness and well-being following the intervention.

Research and
public engagement

The trailer will also host conversations and short talks about light and circadian rhythms.

These activities are intended for the wider public as well as study participants. The mobile infrastructure builds on the “Nachtmensch oder Frühaufsteher?” science roadshow.

Planned outputs include methodological work on adaptive field interventions and empirical analyses of how light conditions relate to circadian, sleep and cognitive outcomes.
